title: Introduce model latency signatures and alert burst-dampener
author: Lena Ortiz
release_notes: Adds per-model latency signature collection and a burst-dampener aggregation rule to reduce alert noise. Includes new dashboard panels and an opt-in runtime flag. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: We see frequent short-lived latency spikes from certain models (especially larger context workloads) that trigger noisy alerts and obscure persistent degradations. This PR adds two complementary features: 1) model latency signatures — compact percentile fingerprints split by model, sequence-length band, and hardware tier for easier anomaly detection; 2) an alert burst-dampener — a temporal aggregator that compresses flapping hits into a single alert window to reduce noise and pager fatigue.

What this changes:
- A new collector (observability/collector/latency_signatures_collector.go) that computes incremental percentile sketches (P2/sketch) per model+seq-band every minute and emits compact metrics "redwood.latency.signature" with labels {model, seq_band, hw_tier, window}. The sketches are small (<=256 bytes) and are meant for rollup pipelines, not raw-token payloads.
- A short-lived in-memory reservoir summarizer used by the collector to stabilize percentiles across minute boundaries.
- Console/dashboard: added two panels: "Latency Signatures by Model" (visualizes the 50/95/99 fingerprints across seq bands) and "Signature Drift" (shows cosine distance between current and baseline signatures). Files: console/dashboards/latency_signatures_panel.json, console/dashboards/signature_drift_panel.json.
- Alerts: new alert rule alerts/burst_dampener_rule.yml that wraps existing per-route latency SLO checks with a dampener policy. The policy groups triggers by model+route and compresses any series of hits within a rolling 3-minute window into a single alert event, while still recording the original hit timestamps in a condensed annotation for debugging.
- Runtime flag: OBS_ENABLE_SIGNATURES=true|false; default false for gradual rollout. Also a config knob OBS_BURST_DAMPEN_WINDOW (default 3m) for ops tuning.

Design notes:
- Signatures are not intended for per-invocation attribution; they are compact aggregated summaries to help triage which model/seq-band deviated. We intentionally do not attach them to traces to avoid increasing trace payloads.
- The dampener operates at the alerting layer (Prometheus/Alertmanager wrapper) to be deployment-agnostic; it emits a synthetic annotation event to the primary alert so runbooks still get a timeline.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for the sketch update/merge logic and serializer (pkg/observability/sketch_test.go).
- Integration test that runs a synthetic workload generator (perf/bench/signature_gen.py) to validate signature stability across noise and verifies the dampener coalesces bursts into a single alert (tests/integration/dampener_integration_test.sh).
- Manual verification steps included in the PR checklist below.

Checklist: 
- [x] Collector implementation and unit tests
- [x] Dashboard JSON and console wiring
- [x] Dampener rule and integration test
- [x] Runtime flags and config docs (docs/observability/signature_and_dampener.md)
- [x] Updated runbook snippets for alerts (docs/runbooks/latency_dampener.adoc)
- [x] Validate that metrics cardinality stays bounded by seq-band bucketing and model allowlist

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (OBS_ENABLE_SIGNATURES=false).
2) Flip to true for internal prod namespace for 24h with signature export disabled to confirm low overhead.
3) Enable signatures + dampener in a canary namespace and monitor signature drift and alert rate.
4) Gradually expand to all namespaces if stable.

Backwards compatibility and migration:
- No schema change to public APIs. Metric name is additive. Alert dampener is non-destructive and configurable.

CI summary: All CI jobs passed after a flaky integration test was fixed (rerun). Checks: unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, linter: pass, dashboard-lint: pass.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals and a green CI run.

Why this is different: Prior observability PRs focused heavily on token-cost attributions and span rollups. This change introduces a compact, model-scoped latency fingerprinting mechanism combined with an alert-layer dampener to reduce noise rather than increasing sampling. The combination helps SREs prioritize persistent regressions over transient resource-constrained spikes.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4301: auto-baselining of signatures per model to propose SLO adjustments (follow-up PR).
- Dashboard UX: add a guided diff tool to compare signatures across releases.
